newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: ANZ Investment Bank sees further mandates.
newsitem.headline: ANZ Investment Bank sees further mandates.

text.p: ANZ Investment Bank said on Thursday that it hoped to be mandated for further sovereign issues following its successful launch of an issue for Pakistan earlier this week.

Mark Coombs, Global Head of Finanical Markets at ANZ Investment Bank, told Reuters that he saw one or two opportunities for sovereign or very close to sovereign borrowers that he hoped to be roadshowing this year.
"I hope we are going to see a couple of mandates now to put together for issue before the end of the northern hemisphere summer," he said.
The bank lead-managed its first sovereign issue in international markets this week. Coombs said this was the first by an Australian bank in recent history.
The Pakistan floating note rate issue came as a US$300 million offering, three-times larger than was originally planned and saw a wide sweep of international interest.

"We have managed to get a major sovereign from a significantly less than investment grade country sold into offshore management accounts...and professional fund managers in the Asian region too, that haven't looked at below investment grade paper," Coombs said.
Pakistan is rated B2 by Moody's Investors Service.
Coombs, who is based in London, is currently in Sydney as part of the bank's commitment to building up interest in credit spread issuance and trading.

ANZ Investment Bank, which is a unit of the Melbourne-based big four bank Australia and New Zealand Banking Group Ltd, has put in place a research team in Sydney to analyse credit and "for this market we see credit spread growing very rapidly".
He said Australian investors to date have been fairly conservative in their approach to credit risk, sticking to investments that are in the top tier of credit risk.
"It's a new departure for Australian investors. But they are doing the right thing, they are taking their time, they are beginning to understand it professionally."

"We are doing analysis and saying -- look don't mess around in double-A, have a look at triple-B. Start thinking about BBB and the value, and how basically you are getting paid far too much for what is not really that lower credit," he added.
